chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far saying:

If people knew what the Qa'im would do when he appears, most of them would wish they did not see him, because of the number of people he kills. Indeed, he will begin only with Quraysh, so he will take from them nothing but the sword, and give them nothing but the sword, until many people say: 'This is not from the Family of Muhammad.' And if he were from the Family of Muhammad, he would be merciful.

key_terms.السَّيْفَ: The sword, symbolizing military conquest and authority
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qa'im (The Raiser/Imam), a title for the Twelfth Imam in Shia eschatology
key_terms.قُرَيْشٌ: Quraysh, the tribe of the Prophet Muhammad

ai.seo_question: Why will people doubt the Qa'im's lineage according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) elucidates that the Qa'im will initially target Quraysh with the sword, a decisive military action that will provoke widespread doubt among the masses who, expecting familial mercy, will question his lineage. This narrative highlights the theme of 'ghurba' (alienation) and the necessity of divine justice over popular sentiment, a core concept in Shia eschatology regarding the Mahdi's rise. The reference to Quraysh specifically underscores the historical and political weight of this tribe in early Islamic history, making their subjugation a significant sign of his authority.
